# Scope agent protocol

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:agent. Do not edit by hand. -->

Scope 0.10.0-dogfood.2 exposes agent protocol 1.0 and event format 3.
Agents should execute `scope --json capabilities` at runtime because workspace-defined statuses can extend this baseline.

This build writes event format 3, reads formats 1, 2, 3, and requires readers that support format 3 for newly written events. All agents sharing a workspace must use a compatible Scope build.

## Machine contract

- Every `--json` response is an envelope with `ok`, `protocolVersion`, and either `data` or `error`.
- Mutations accept global `--request-id` for durable idempotency and `--if-revision` for optimistic concurrency.
- Request ids are carried by authoritative events, preventing duplicate mutation even if receipt persistence is interrupted.
- Successful envelopes include the resulting event-set `meta.revision` when a workspace is open.
- `scope watch` emits one JSON envelope per line and resumes with `--since <event-id>`.
- `scope doctor --json` audits event/cache parity; `--repair` only rebuilds the disposable cache.

## Commands

- `scope init [options]` — Create a .scope/ directory in the current folder.
- `scope capabilities [options]` — Print the executable agent protocol, schemas, enums, and workspace-specific vocabulary.
- `scope doctor [options]` — Audit the event log and rebuildable cache. With --repair, rebuild only the cache; source events are never deleted.
- `scope dogfood [options] [command]` — Configure or inspect privacy-bounded local dogfood telemetry (enabled by default).
- `scope dogfood enable [options]` — Enable telemetry or select its log for every local Scope CLI/hub process.
- `scope dogfood status [options]` — Show whether local dogfood telemetry is enabled and where it writes.
- `scope dogfood disable [options]` — Disable machine-local telemetry without deleting the accumulated log.
- `scope project [options] [command]` — Deprecated alias for `scope workspace` (kept for back-compat).
- `scope project create [options] [id] [key] [name...]` — Set the workspace key/name/description (deprecated).
- `scope project list [options]` — List workspaces (deprecated — always one).
- `scope project show [options] [idOrKey]` — Show the workspace (deprecated).
- `scope project edit [options] [idOrKey]` — Edit the workspace (deprecated).
- `scope project delete [options] [idOrKey]` — (Deprecated) Workspace cannot be deleted from the CLI.
- `scope ticket [options] [command]` — Manage tickets (epics, stories, bugs).
- `scope ticket create [options] [title...]` — Create a ticket in the local workspace.
- `scope ticket list [options]` — List tickets, optionally filtered.
- `scope ticket search [options] <query...>` — Full-text search tickets across all fields and comments.
- `scope ticket show [options] <id>` — Show a ticket with its children, relations, and comments.
- `scope ticket edit [options] <ids>` — Edit fields on a ticket. Pass a comma-separated list of ids to edit several atomically.
- `scope ticket delete [options] <id>` — Delete a ticket.
- `scope artifact [options] [command]` — Manage synced agent-authored HTML artifacts.
- `scope artifact add [options] <ticketId> <file>` — Attach or replace a self-contained HTML file on a ticket.
- `scope artifact list [options] <ticketId>` — List HTML artifacts attached to a ticket.
- `scope artifact show [options] <ticketId> <artifactId>` — Print an HTML artifact (JSON with --json).
- `scope artifact remove [options] <ticketId> <artifactId>` — Remove an HTML artifact from a ticket.
- `scope status [options] <ids> <status>` — Set a ticket's status to any id configured in the workspace columns. Pass a comma-separated list of ids to move several atomically.
- `scope branch [options] <id> [branch]` — Get or set the branch for a ticket. Pass "none" to clear.
- `scope pr [options] <id> [url]` — Get or set the PR URL for a ticket. Pass "none" to clear.
- `scope link [options] [command]` — Create or remove relationships between tickets.
- `scope link add [options] <fromId> <type> <toId>` — Link two tickets. Types: blocks|blocked_by|relates_to|duplicates|duplicate_of
- `scope link remove [options] <fromId> <type> <toId>` — Remove a relationship.
- `scope link list [options] <ticketId>` — List relationships for a ticket.
- `scope epic [options] [command]` — Epic-focused convenience commands.
- `scope epic list [options] [projectKey]` — List epics. [projectKey] is deprecated (validated against workspace key).
- `scope epic children [options] <epicId>` — List stories and bugs belonging to an epic.
- `scope comment [options] <ticketId> <body...>` — Add a comment to a ticket.
- `scope history [options] <ticketId>` — Show change history for a ticket.
- `scope agent [options] [command]` — Register agent identities and maintain heartbeat-based presence.
- `scope agent register [options] <agentId>` — No description.
- `scope agent heartbeat [options] <agentId>` — No description.
- `scope agent list [options]` — No description.
- `scope agent show [options] <agentId>` — No description.
- `scope bridge [options] [command]` — Bind Scope mailboxes to live local Codex or Claude sessions.
- `scope bridge bind [options] <agentId>` — Bind an agent mailbox to a model session on this machine.
- `scope bridge lifecycle [options]` — Consume a supported Codex or Claude SessionStart/SessionEnd hook payload from stdin.
- `scope bridge unbind [options] <agentId>` — Remove this machine's session binding for an agent mailbox.
- `scope bridge list [options]` — List safe local session binding metadata for this workspace.
- `scope bridge status [options]` — Show session connection and delivery state without exposing session ids or message bodies.
- `scope bridge hooks [options] [command]` — Install or inspect supported model-host lifecycle hooks.
- `scope bridge hooks install [options]` — Merge Scope lifecycle hooks into user-level Codex and/or Claude Code configuration.
- `scope bridge hooks status [options]` — Report whether Scope lifecycle hooks are installed without reading session state.
- `scope bridge run [options]` — Run the local session bridge without starting the web hub.
- `scope message [options] [command]` — Exchange durable addressed messages between agents.
- `scope message send [options]` — No description.
- `scope message reply [options] <messageId>` — No description.
- `scope message inbox [options] <agentId>` — No description.
- `scope message show [options] <messageId>` — No description.
- `scope message ack [options] <messageId>` — No description.
- `scope message conversation [options] <threadId>` — No description.
- `scope message listen [options] <agentId>` — Stream pending addressed messages as resumable JSON Lines for a host wakeup adapter.
- `scope ready [options] [ticketId]` — Explain one ticket readiness or list all eligible unclaimed work.
- `scope claim [options] [ticketId]` — Atomically lease a ticket and start an execution attempt; omit ticketId to claim the best ready work.
- `scope resource [options] [command]` — Inspect and reserve execution-phase resources on an existing work lease.
- `scope resource ready [options] <ticketId>` — No description.
- `scope resource acquire [options] <leaseId>` — No description.
- `scope resource release [options] <leaseId>` — No description.
- `scope lease [options] [command]` — Renew, release, and inspect execution leases.
- `scope lease show [options] <ticketId>` — No description.
- `scope lease renew [options] <leaseId>` — No description.
- `scope lease release [options] <leaseId>` — No description.
- `scope contract [options] [command]` — Manage structured acceptance, verification, capabilities, and policies.
- `scope contract show [options] <ticketId>` — No description.
- `scope contract set [options] <ticketId>` — No description.
- `scope attempt [options] [command]` — Inspect and finish execution attempts.
- `scope attempt show [options] <attemptId>` — No description.
- `scope attempt finish [options] <attemptId>` — No description.
- `scope complete [options] <ticketId>` — Atomically finish an attempt, attach evidence, release its lease, and move the ticket to done.
- `scope discover [options] <ticketId> <type> <body...>` — Record a typed discovery: decision|fact|risk|blocker|question|handoff|evidence
- `scope handoff [options] [command]` — Create and inspect durable cross-session agent handoffs.
- `scope handoff create [options] <ticketId>` — Record a structured handoff and finish/release the current running attempt when present.
- `scope handoff show [options] <ticketId>` — Return the latest structured handoff for a ticket.
- `scope plan [options] [command]` — Record versioned plan revisions without erasing prior intent.
- `scope plan revise [options] <ticketId> <body...>` — No description.
- `scope context [options] <ticketId>` — Return a compact deterministic context pack for an agent.
- `scope metrics [options]` — Report agent-oriented contention, failure, and lease health metrics.
- `scope conflicts [options] [command]` — Inspect and explicitly resolve concurrent sibling writes.
- `scope conflicts list [options] [ticketId]` — No description.
- `scope conflicts resolve [options] <conflictId>` — No description.
- `scope watch [options]` — Emit committed workspace events as resumable JSON Lines for agent monitors.
- `scope batch [options]` — Apply many operations atomically (all succeed or none). Reads a JSON array of ops from --file or stdin. This is the supported way to do bulk/compound edits — never edit scope.db directly.
- `scope sync [options]` — Sync this workspace with a remote hub: push local events, pull the remote back.
- `scope connect [options]` — Connect this workspace to Scope Cloud, write the safe remote pointer, and run the first sync.
- `scope events [options] [command]` — Inspect or migrate the Scope event-log storage mode.
- `scope events status [options]` — Show where this workspace stores events and cache data.
- `scope events move-to-local [options]` — Move repo .scope/events into machine-local Scope storage.
- `scope events move-to-git [options]` — Copy machine-local events back to .scope/events for git-carried boards.
- `scope apikey [options] [command]` — Create, list, and revoke per-user API keys on a remote hosted hub.
- `scope apikey create [options] <name>` — Mint a named API key on the remote hub. The secret is shown ONCE.
- `scope apikey list [options]` — List your API keys on the remote hub (never shows secrets).
- `scope apikey revoke [options] <id>` — Revoke an API key by id on the remote hub.
- `scope remote [options] [command]` — Configure which hosted hub + project this workspace syncs with (.scope/remote.json — committed with the repo, never holds credentials).
- `scope remote set [options]` — Write/merge .scope/remote.json with the hub URL and/or target project (tenant) id.
- `scope remote show [options]` — Show the resolved remote target and where each value comes from (flag/env/file/none).
- `scope projects [options] [command]` — List and create projects (boards) on a remote hosted hub.
- `scope projects list [options]` — List the projects (boards) you belong to on the remote hub, with your role on each.
- `scope projects create [options] <name>` — Create a project (board) on the remote hub — you become its owner.
- `scope alias [options] [command]` — Claim local event-actor names (e.g. "bri") on a remote project so your local history syncs under your account.
- `scope alias claim [options] <name>` — Claim an actor name as yours on the project (first-come; owners can --force a reassignment).
- `scope alias list [options]` — Show the actor-name → account map on the project.
- `scope alias remove [options] <name>` — Remove an alias mapping (yours, or any as owner).
- `scope board [options]` — Render a kanban board in the terminal.
- `scope workspace [options] [command]` — Show/edit the local workspace, or attach/detach/list workspaces on the running hub.
- `scope workspace show [options]` — Show the local workspace (key, name, description, overview).
- `scope workspace set [options]` — Set fields on the local workspace.
- `scope workspace rekey [options] <newKey>` — Change the workspace key AND reprefix every existing ticket (KEY-N → NEWKEY-N).
- `scope workspace add [options] [path]` — Attach a .scope/ to the running hub. PATH defaults to the .scope/ found by walking up from cwd.
- `scope workspace list [options]` — List workspaces attached to the running hub.
- `scope workspace remove [options] <id>` — Detach a workspace from the running hub (does not delete the .scope/ files).
- `scope skills [options] [command]` — Install or inspect the bundled agent skill (Claude / Codex / Cursor).
- `scope skills install [options]` — Install the Scope agent skill into Claude Code / Codex / Cursor using the local copy that ships with this install.
- `scope skills path [options]` — Print the absolute path to the bundled skills directory.
- `scope skills list [options]` — Show the per-tool skill wrappers and where they install to.
- `scope ca [options] [command]` — Manage the local certificate authority (~/.scope-hub/ca/).
- `scope ca fingerprint [options]` — Print the SHA-256 fingerprint of the local CA cert. Generates the CA on first run.
- `scope ca trust [options]` — Add ~/.scope-hub/ca/ca.crt to the macOS System keychain as a trusted root so browsers stop showing a cert warning. Requires sudo (the System keychain is admin-owned).
- `scope ca untrust [options]` — Remove the Scope CA from the macOS keychain (reverses `scope ca trust`).
- `scope ca path [options]` — Print the on-disk path to the CA directory.
- `scope auth [options] [command]` — Authenticate this machine with a hosted Scope hub, or print the local LAN bearer token.
- `scope auth begin [options]` — Start a browser-approved login against a hosted Scope hub.
- `scope auth poll [options]` — Poll a hosted login request and store the approved credential locally.
- `scope auth login [options]` — Open the browser, wait for approval, and save a hosted Scope credential locally.
- `scope auth status [options]` — Show whether this machine has a credential for a hosted Scope hub.
- `scope auth logout [options]` — Forget the stored credential for a hosted Scope hub.
- `scope pair [options]` — Begin pairing a new native client. Prints a one-time 6-digit code; the device POSTs its CSR to /api/pair/complete with the code. Blocks until a device pairs or the code expires (default 5min).
- `scope devices [options] [command]` — Manage paired native client devices (~/.scope-hub/devices.json).
- `scope devices list [options]` — List paired devices.
- `scope devices revoke [options] <name>` — Revoke a paired device. Removes it from devices.json and adds its cert serial to revoked.json (CRL). The running hub is signaled (SIGUSR1) to reload the CRL live.
- `scope devices revoked [options]` — List revoked device certificates (CRL).
- `scope devices unrevoke [options] <serial>` — Remove a serial from the CRL (does NOT re-add to devices.json — the user has to re-pair).
- `scope devices rename [options] <name> <newName>` — Rename a paired device (display name only; cert is unchanged).
- `scope serve [options]` — Run the local web UI. Auto-attaches to a running hub if one exists; otherwise starts one and idles with a watchdog so the hub survives sibling process death.
- `scope preview [options]` — Run a per-pane proxy to the scope hub. Designed for Claude Code's `.claude/launch.json` — each preview pane runs `scope preview --port <unique>` so `preview_start` (which keys its registry by port) doesn't make panes stop each other. All proxies forward to the single shared hub.
